labels: Some of Slides are picked from
UVA Deep Learning Course   EFSTRATIOS GAVVES

layout.arrangement: Title-only section slide: thin dark-red rectangular border frames the whole slide; large multi-line title centered horizontally in the upper-middle area; small italic two-line attribution note in the bottom-left corner; a mouse cursor arrow floats near the bottom-left above the attribution; a solid black bar runs along the very bottom edge of the frame (video letterboxing/controls strip).

regions.name: Framed slide canvas
regions.position: center, roughly x 6%-95%, y 8%-97% of frame
regions.content: Light gray slide surface enclosed by a thin dark-red border line

regions.name: Title block
regions.position: top-middle to middle, horizontally centered, y ~18%-60% of slide
regions.content: Three centered lines of large bold dark-red text: 'Introduction to' / 'Convolutional Neural Network' / '(CNN)'

regions.name: Attribution note
regions.content: Two lines of small italic dark text crediting the source course and author

regions.name: Mouse cursor
regions.position: bottom-left area, x ~29%, y ~85% of slide
regions.content: Standard white/black arrow mouse pointer captured from the screen recording

regions.name: Bottom black bar
regions.content: Solid black horizontal strip (video player/letterbox artifact, not slide content)

layout.hierarchy: The huge bold dark-red title dominates absolutely; everything else (thin border, tiny italic footnote) is subordinate. Visual order: title >> red border frame > attribution text > cursor.

visual_elements.description: Thin rectangular border (approximately 1-2 px stroke) framing the entire slide content area with no fill; acts as a decorative frame around all content.
visual_elements.position: Full slide perimeter, inset slightly from the frame edges

visual_elements.description: Mouse cursor arrow (standard pointer with white fill and black outline) captured mid-recording, angled up-left, located just above the attribution text.
visual_elements.position: Bottom-left quadrant, above the attribution lines

imagery: No photos, icons, or illustrations besides the incidental mouse-pointer cursor from the screen capture
typography_notes: Title: very large, bold, sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica-like), dark red, centered, set on three lines with generous line spacing ('Introduction to' slightly smaller than the following two lines, which share the largest size). Attribution: small italic sans-serif, dark gray/black, sentence case, two lines, left-aligned. No all-caps, no numbered or bulleted lists anywhere on the slide.
animation_state: No build state visible; slide appears fully rendered as a static section-title slide. The only transient artifact is the recorded mouse cursor near the bottom-left.
recreation_brief: 1. Create a new 16:9 PowerPoint slide and set the background fill to light gray (#E9E9E7).
2. Draw a rectangle with No Fill and a solid dark-red (#A6191E) outline of ~1.5 pt covering the entire slide with a small margin (~0.15 in) on all sides, to reproduce the thin red frame.

3. Insert a centered text box spanning roughly x 10%-90%, y 15%-65%. Type three centered lines in bold dark-red (#A6191E) sans-serif (e.g., Arial Bold): line 1 'Introduction to' at ~40 pt; line 2 'Convolutional Neural Network' at ~48 pt; line 3 '(CNN)' at ~48 pt. Add paragraph spacing between lines so they breathe like the original.

4. Insert a small text box in the bottom-left corner (approx. x 10%, y 87%). Type two left-aligned italic lines in dark gray (#3A3A3A), ~12 pt: line 1 'Some of Slides are picked from'; line 2 'UVA Deep Learning Course   EFSTRATIOS GAVVES' (keep the wide gap between 'Course' and 'EFSTRATIOS').

5. Optionally add a small arrow cursor image (white arrow with black outline) just above the attribution box at ~x 29%, y 84% only if pixel-perfect fidelity to the video frame is desired; otherwise omit as it is a recording artifact.
6. Do not add any bullets, charts, or images; the slide is a pure section-title slide. Ignore the black strip at the very bottom of the source image (video player artifact).
